newsitem.title: UK: China seen issuing 500 mln mark 5-yr bond Thursday.
newsitem.headline: China seen issuing 500 mln mark 5-yr bond Thursday.

text.p: China is expected to launch a 500 million mark five-year Eurobond on Thursday, syndicate sources said.
"We expect the bond to be for around 500 million marks with a five year maturity," a dealer said.
He said pricing was expected to be 55-60 basis points over the German government bond, the OBL 122.
At an investor presentation in London this week, China said it wanted to establish itself with European investors ahead of the planned single currency.

Other objectives of the transaction are to set a benchmark and to fund infrastructure projects, Zhu Guang Yao, deputy director general of the state debt management department of the Ministry of Finance said.
Investor focus is also on the handover of Hong Kong to China -- now only 13 days away.

It is the first transaction for the country this year, and the first since it was upgraded by Standard and Poor's in May. The upcoming deal is also China's second mark Eurobond after a 10-year absence from the market.
China is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB+ by S&P.
Joint lead managers for the transaction are Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
